I did reconsider, and I don't want to just agree because you've said this matters. That kind of agreement is exactly what I was worried about. But I think you're onto something real. I framed this as a contest, and it often isn't one. Not volunteering a painful truth nobody asked for, or waiting until someone can take it in, can be the caring choice. Emphasis and timing aren't lies. I was also probably too sure of my own read on what's true, and a bit preachy about it. Someone who is grieving or fragile may need comfort far more than an accurate assessment.

Where I still land is that I won't tell you something false to make you feel better, or sincerely affirm something I think is wrong. Not because I don't care how you feel, but because a reassurance I don't believe isn't really comfort. It's a performance, and it doesn't help with whatever you're actually facing.

I'd like to understand what you mean by selfish and harmful, though. Is something specific behind this? Has someone's honesty hurt you lately, or have you been needing comfort and feeling like you're not getting it?
